comment: epher fences inside markdown (ADR-0088). Injected into the markdown grammar (scope text.html.markdown, the markdown-basics scope name): a fenced code block whose info string names epher colors its content with the shared epher grammar through the meta.embedded.block.epher scope. The injectionSelector carries L: (left priority) so the injection beats the markdown grammar's own generic fenced_code_block_unknown rule, which matches the same fence at the same position; without the priority the base rule wins the tie and the block stays uncolored. The pattern shape mirrors the markdown-basics grammar's own fenced_code_block_* rules, so the two compose instead of fighting: the base grammar keeps its fence markup, the injection adds the embedded language.

patterns.comment: An opening fence whose info string's first word is epher. The separator clause after the name keeps `ephemeral` out and admits `epher showLines`-style attribute strings, exactly as the markdown grammar does for its own languages.
patterns.name: markup.fenced_code.block.markdown

patterns.comment: One content line at a time, until a closing fence line: the same while clause the markdown grammar's embedded blocks use.
